profile.name: subscriber1
profile.preferences: I'm into space tech and rocket launches. I want the real engineering moments: engine ignition, liftoff, booster and stage separation, and how the vehicle is performing. I prefer live footage over animations. Skip the studio chat, crowd shots and interviews. Keep it around two minutes.

title: Artemis I Night Launch - SLS and Orion to the Moon
recap: You get RS-25 ignition through liftoff, throttling through Max Q, booster jettison and fairing separation plus the gimbal steering test. All clips use live pad and tracking views showing thrust, speed and staging as it happened.

clips.title: RS-25 gimbal steering test
clips.subject: engine
clips.reason: Real engineering moment in terminal count live: close-up of four RS-25 nozzles gimballing to test steering before launch.

clips.title: Engine ignition and liftoff
clips.subject: rocket
clips.reason: Core request for engine ignition and liftoff in live footage, with hydrogen burnoff igniters, RS-25 start, booster ignition and night liftoff at excitement 9-10.

clips.title: Engines throttle through Max Q
clips.subject: plume
clips.reason: Shows how vehicle is performing live: four core engines throttling down for Max Q then back to maximum thrust at 1,420 mph.

clips.title: Solid rocket booster separation
clips.subject: flame
clips.reason: Core request for booster separation live, showing twin 177-foot boosters cutting off and jettisoning with two plumes moving apart at excitement 8-9.

clips.title: Service module fairing separation
clips.subject: screen
clips.reason: Covers stage separation request with onboard VIS-FOV view and confirmation that service module fairing panels separated about 3 minutes into flight.

verification.shows: Live close-up of four RS-25 engines gimballing on the SLS core stage during terminal count
Live nighttime footage of SLS RS-25 engine and booster ignition with hydrogen burnoff, followed by liftoff and ascent
A rocket ascends at night with a bright engine plume while flight commentary describes four core engines throttling down for Max Q and back to maximum thrust
Live nighttime footage of twin solid rocket boosters separating from the core stage with two bright plumes moving apart
Onboard VIS-FOV live camera shows service module fairing panels separating with telemetry overlay and voice confirmation about 3 minutes into flight
